## Purpose and scope

This protocol extracts total RNA from whole honey bees and from isopod hepatopancreas, for gene expression and other RNA-based analyses. Both sample types use TRIzol homogenisation and chloroform phase separation; the aqueous phase is then cleaned on a spin column. The two source protocols use different column kits, so the clean-up is given separately for each sample type (A: bees; B: isopod hepatopancreas). Other sample types need validation.

## Principle

TRIzol (phenol and guanidine isothiocyanate) lyses the tissue and keeps RNA intact. After chloroform is added and the sample is centrifuged, the mixture separates into a pink organic phase at the bottom, a white interphase and a colourless aqueous phase at the top, which contains the RNA. The aqueous phase is mixed with cold 70% ethanol and bound to a silica column; the column is washed (bees: with on-column DNase digestion), dried, and RNA is eluted in RNase-free water.

## Reagent preparation

- **Ethanol 70%:** pre-cooled in the freezer [TO CONFIRM: preparation with RNase-free water].
- **DNase digestion mix (bees):** per sample, 90 µL Buffer DI + 10 µL DNase I; prepare during step A.
- **Kit buffers:** prepare as stated on the bottles (e.g. ethanol added to wash buffers) [TO CONFIRM].

**Differences between the two sample types**

<!-- bench -->
**Sample-type settings.**

| Step | A. Bees | B. Isopod hepatopancreas |
|:--|:--|:--|
| TRIzol | 300–500 µL | 300 µL |
| Homogenisation | Bead beating 6.5 m/s, 2 × 30 s | Mechanical homogeniser; then 5 min at room temperature |
| Chloroform | 200 µL, mix by pipetting | 150 µL, vortex |
| Phase separation | 14 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C | 15 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C |
| Cold 70% ethanol | 350 µL | 250 µL |
| Column kit | NZY Total RNA (NI, DNase, NWR1, NWR2) | RNeasy-type (RW1, RPE) |

## Procedure

### Before starting

- Set the centrifuge to 4 °C.
- Clean the bench and work with RNase-free tubes and filter tips [TO CONFIRM].

### A. Honey bees

(@) Put 300–500 µL of TRIzol and the bee in a tube with beads.
(@) Homogenise in the bead-beating machine at 6.5 m/s for 30 s, twice.
(@) Centrifuge at 4 000 × g for 3 min at 4 °C.
(@) Transfer the liquid to a new tube for the chloroform step [TO CONFIRM: volume transferred].
(@) Add 200 µL of chloroform and mix well by pipetting.
(@) Incubate for 3 min at room temperature.
(@) Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C. Three phases form (pink at the bottom, a white layer in the middle and a colourless supernatant on top); take as much of the upper phase as possible.
(@) Add the upper phase to 350 µL of cold 70% ethanol and pipette up and down.
(@) Change gloves.
(@) Transfer to the (blue) column and centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 s. If needed, load the sample in portions of 500 µL. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 350 µL of Buffer NI and centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 s. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Prepare the DNase digestion mix (90 µL DI + 10 µL DNase I per sample). Add 95 µL to the column and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
(@) Add 200 µL of Buffer NWR1, centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min and discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 600 µL of Buffer NWR2, centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min and discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 250 µL of Buffer NWR2, centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min and discard the flow-through.
(@) Place the column in a new microtube and centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 2 min to remove residual buffer.
(@) Place the column in a new microtube, add 20 µL of RNase-free water to the column and wait 1 min.
(@) Change gloves. Centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min: the eluate is sample 1.
(@) Place the column in a new microtube, add 20 µL of RNase-free water and wait 1 min. Centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 1 min: the eluate is sample 2.
(@) Measure concentration and quality on the NanoDrop (EnGeL-MOLB-NAQC).

### B. Isopod hepatopancreas

(@) Homogenise the hepatopancreas in 300 µL of TRIzol in a mechanical homogeniser.
(@) Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
(@) Add 150 µL of chloroform and vortex well.
(@) Incubate for 3 min at room temperature.
(@) Centrifuge at 15 000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C. Three phases form (pink at the bottom, a white layer in the middle and a colourless supernatant on top); take as much of the upper phase as possible.
(@) Add the upper phase to 250 µL of cold 70% ethanol and pipette up and down.
(@) Transfer to the column and centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 10 s. If needed, load in portions of 500 µL. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 700 µL of 100% ethanol and centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 15 s. Discard the flow-through. This extra wash is intended (lab practice); it is not part of the standard RNeasy procedure.
(@) Add 700 µL of Buffer RW1 and centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 15 s. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 500 µL of Buffer RPE and centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 15 s. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Add 500 µL of Buffer RPE and centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 3 min. Discard the flow-through.
(@) Place the column in a new microtube and centrifuge at ≥ 12 000 × g (microcentrifuge, 1.5 mL tube rotor) for 2 min to remove residual buffer.
(@) Place the column in a new microtube, add 20 µL of RNase-free water and wait 1 min. Centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 15 s: the eluate is sample 1.
(@) Place the column in a new microtube, add 20 µL of RNase-free water and wait 1 min. Centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 15 s: the eluate is sample 2.
(@) Measure concentration and quality on the NanoDrop (EnGeL-MOLB-NAQC).

### RNA storage

(@) Store the RNA at [TO CONFIRM: −80 °C?] until use.

## Calculations

Not applicable: volumes are per sample. For $n$ samples, prepare $V = v \times n \times 1.1$ of each solution ($v$: volume per sample, µL; 1.1: 10% excess).

## Quality control

| Control | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| RNA purity (NanoDrop A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~) | Protein, phenol or salt carry-over | [TO CONFIRM] |
| RNA concentration | Enough RNA for downstream use | [TO CONFIRM] |
| RNA integrity | Degradation | [TO CONFIRM: e.g. TapeStation RNA ScreenTape, used in the lab?] |
| Extraction blank | Contamination | [TO CONFIRM: used?] |

## Data and metadata

- **Sample labels:** EnGeL labels from the sample master data file; each RNA extract gets its own code (sample nature `RNA`), with the source sample code in a separate column. Sample 1 and sample 2 (two elutions) are recorded separately [TO CONFIRM: or pooled].
- **Where:** [TO CONFIRM: project records] and the lab book.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- EnGeL labels of the source sample and of each eluate
- Sample type (A or B); extraction date; operator; TRIzol and column-kit lot numbers
- Concentration, A~260~/A~280~ and A~260~/A~230~ of each eluate
:::

## Safety and waste

{{< include ../../includes/_safety-general.qmd >}}

- TRIzol contains phenol and guanidine isothiocyanate: toxic and corrosive; avoid skin contact and inhalation [TO CONFIRM against the SDS; work in the fume hood?].
- Chloroform: harmful if inhaled or swallowed; suspected carcinogen [TO CONFIRM against the SDS].
{{< include ../../includes/_safety-guanidine.qmd >}}
{{< include ../../includes/_safety-ethanol.qmd >}}

**Waste**

{{< include ../../includes/_waste-streams.qmd >}}

For this protocol: the organic phase and interphase (TRIzol, chloroform) [TO CONFIRM: waste route; halogenated solvent waste is not one of the three EnGeL streams]; column flow-through to biological liquid waste (jerrican), never with bleach; tubes, columns and tips to biological solid waste (black bin).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Sample does not fit the column | Large aqueous phase + ethanol volume | Load in portions of 500 µL. |
| Low A~260~/A~230~ | Carry-over of TRIzol or salts | [TO CONFIRM] |
| Genomic DNA in the RNA (isopods) | No DNase step in path B | [TO CONFIRM: add on-column DNase?] |

## Remarks

The source protocols are in Portuguese; this version is a translation that keeps their steps and values. The Roslin SOP for RNA isolation from frozen tissue is in the source folder for reference.

## References

Qiagen (2006). RNeasy Mini Handbook (04/2006): 8 000 × g (10 000 rpm) for loading, washes and elution; full speed for the dry spin.
